title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' study, a self-made reformulation of the defining relations of what is now called the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Here π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on two generators. The symbols ρ (order 3, cyclically permuting 0,1,∞) and σ_∞ (order 2, fixing ∞ and swapping 0,1) are the automorphisms induced by the S_3-symmetries, viewed as elements of an extension of π̂_{0,3}. Write τ_∞ for the extra element used to enlarge the group to π̂_{0,3}^~ = π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞}. The objects u ∈ M^{!~}_{0,3} are automorphisms of this structure. On the previous pages each u is encoded by a triple (g,h,f) with u(ρ)=gρ and u(σ_∞)=hσ_∞. Condition (25) consists of the cocycle conditions on g and h for the actions of Z/3 and Z/2. Condition (29) is the loop relation σ_∞(h)g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f), where ν=(μ−1)/2 and μ is the cyclotomic multiplier.

Step 1, equation (31)–(32). Grothendieck trivialises the cocycles: g = α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1} = [α_0,ρ] and h = β_0σ_∞(β_0)^{-1} = [β_0,σ_∞]. Here β_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}, but α_0 must be allowed to range over π̂_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞}. In modern terms this is a computation of nonabelian H^1.
- H^1(Z/2, π̂_{0,3}) is trivial. The quotient orbifold by σ_∞ has π_1 ≅ Z * Z/2, so there is a single conjugacy class of order-2 lifts.
- H^1(Z/3, π̂_{0,3}) has two classes. The quotient by ρ is a sphere with two cone points of order 3 and one puncture, with π_1 ≅ Z/3 * Z/3, so there are two conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts. The τ_∞ factor reaches the second class.
- Injectivity of (g,h) ↔ (α_0,β_0) needs the fixed subgroups of ρ and σ_∞ in π̂_{0,3} to be trivial, i.e. centralisers of torsion are finite. Profinitely this follows from results on torsion in free profinite products.

Step 2, equation (33)–(34). Substituting into (29), and using σ_∞^2 = 1 so that σ_∞(h) = σ_∞(β_0)β_0^{-1}, gives σ_∞(β_0)β_0^{-1}α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1} = σ_∞(f^{-1}) l_1^ν ρ(f). Multiplying on the left by σ_∞(f) and inserting f^{-1}f gives the boxed (34): (fα_0)ρ(fα_0)^{-1} = ((fβ_0)σ_∞(fβ_0)^{-1}) l_1^ν. The cocycle conditions (25) now hold automatically. The triple depends on f only modulo f ↦ l_0^n f, and ν is determined by (α_0,β_0) via the solvability of (34).

Step 3, next page. Setting α=fα_0 and β=fβ_0 turns (34) into αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} l_1^ν, an equation from which f has been eliminated. The point of the whole page is to rewrite Drinfeld/Ihara-type 2- and 3-cycle relations as a single 'twisted coboundary' equation, parametrising automorphisms by conjugators of the torsion elements ρ and σ_∞.
errors:
The 'correspondance biunivoque' (g,h) ↔ (α_0,β_0) is asserted without proof. It silently uses two non-trivial facts:
- the ρ- and σ_∞-fixed subgroups of π̂_{0,3} are trivial (needed for injectivity);
- the nonabelian H^1 of Z/3 is exactly two classes, reached by {1,τ_∞}, and the H^1 of Z/2 is trivial (needed for surjectivity).
Both are true, by the orbifold/free-product argument (Z/3*Z/3 and Z*Z/2) plus profinite results on torsion in free products, but no argument is given here.

The compatibility of (34) with f ↦ l_0^n f requires ρ(l_0) and σ_∞(l_0) to be the same loop l_1, so that the l_1^{-n} factors commute past l_1^ν. This holds with the stated conventions but is left implicit.
The algebra from (29) to (34) checks out; no computational error found.

ideas.what: Trivialising the cocycles g, h of the Z/3 and Z/2 actions as coboundaries [α_0,ρ], [β_0,σ_∞], enlarging the group by τ_∞ to reach the second Z/3-class.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 of finite cyclic groups acting on free profinite groups, i.e. conjugacy classes of torsion lifts in orbifold fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Serre's nonabelian cohomology); profinite torsion/conjugacy results by Herfort–Ribes and others
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known

ideas.what: Rewriting the GT loop relation as (fα_0)ρ(fα_0)^{-1} = (fβ_0)σ_∞(fβ_0)^{-1} l_1^ν, leading to the f-free equation αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} l_1^ν.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon/pentagon-type relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, written via conjugators of torsion elements (cf. Lochak–Schneps style S_3-orbifold descriptions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for orbifold/torsion presentations
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the Longue Marche manuscript (1981) itself, which is only partially circulated

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms by (α_0,β_0) with u(σ_∞)=int(β_0)σ_∞ and u(ρ)=int(α_0)ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Describing outer automorphisms by their action on the conjugacy classes of finite subgroups (inertia/torsion-preserving automorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in anabelian geometry / GT literature (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps)

missed.claim: The page (with the next one) gives an f-free reformulation of the GT loop relation as a single twisted-coboundary equation. Here α, β are conjugators of the order-3 and order-2 orbifold torsion elements, and the second Z/3 cohomology class is accounted for by τ_∞. I am not aware of this exact parametrisation (α,β) modulo l_0^n in the GT literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It casts the GT relations as a nonabelian-cohomological condition on torsion conjugators. This is the viewpoint later taken in orbifold/stack-theoretic treatments of GT (e.g. via M_{0,4}/S_3 and torsion in mapping class groups). It could give an alternative presentation of GT or of its variants (such as the Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps version).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a competent and careful reformulation of known GT-type relations. The H^1 bookkeeping (the τ_∞ coset) shows real insight into the orbifold structure. But the content is essentially equivalent to known presentations, and I cannot confirm absence from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The first line of the relation reads 'σ_∞(f^{-1}) ℓ_1^ν ρ(f)' (as transcribed); the 'h^ν' visible in the image is a scribble for ℓ_1^ν.
In the second relation, the handwritten argument of ρ(...)^{-1} was corrected to 'fα_0', giving ρ(fα_0)^{-1}, consistent with the underbrace (fβ_0)^{-1}(fα_0).
In (33), the marginal insertion reads 'f déterminé mod f ↦ ℓ_0^n f (n ∈ Ẑ)'. The 'des lacets' insertion belongs to 'la condition des lacets (29)'.
